title: Joyful Song and a Sword
overview: God's faithful people are called to celebrate him with song and dance, and are then pictured carrying out his judgment on hostile nations.

parts.label: A new song together (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The faithful are called to gather and sing a fresh song to God, the one who made Israel as a people and rules them as King. Dancing with hand drums and harps was part of Israel's great celebrations, going back to the songs after the escape from Egypt.

parts.label: Why they celebrate (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: The reason given is that God takes pleasure in his people, a word that can also mean accepting them, and honors the humble with rescue. Singing even while lying in bed may picture joy reaching into private moments, in a place other psalms describe as somewhere people wept.

parts.label: Praise and a sword (vv. 6-8)
parts.note: The singers now also hold double-edged swords to punish other nations and put their kings and nobles in iron chains, and the psalm states this plainly. Interpreters differ on what is in view: some link it to Israel's wars against its neighbors, some to later Jewish revolts against foreign rulers, and many Christians read it as a picture of spiritual struggle.

parts.label: The written sentence (v. 9)
parts.note: The punishment is described as carrying out a judgment already written down, meaning either God's own decision or earlier warnings in Israel's scriptures. Scholars are not sure which is meant, and the psalm calls this task an honor for all the faithful.

disagreement: Christians differ over the sword verses: some read them as a record of ancient Israel's wars against its enemies, while many read them as a picture of spiritual struggle and the final judgment, not a call to physical violence.
think: What do you make of a song that places joyful worship and a call to punish enemies side by side?
